'''Paul Balmer''' (born 1970) is a Swiss mathematician working in tensor triangular geometry, algebraic geometry, modular representation theory, and homotopy theory. He is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of California, Los Angeles]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.math.ucla.edu/~balmer/|title=Home page}}</ref>

Balmer received his [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Lausanne]] in 1998, under the supervision of [[Manuel Ojanguren]], with the thesis ''Groupes de Witt dérivés des Schémas'' (in French).<ref>{{MathGenealogy|id=44976|title=Paul Balmer}}</ref>

His research centers around [[triangulated category|triangulated categories]]. More specifically, he is a proponent of tensor-triangular geometry, an umbrella topic that covers geometric aspects of [[algebraic geometry]], [[modular representation theory]], [[stable homotopy theory]], and other areas, by means of relevant tensor-triangulated categories.

Balmer was an [[List of International Congresses of Mathematicians Plenary and Invited Speakers#2010, Hyderabad|Invited Speaker]] at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Hyderabad]] in 2010, with a talk on ''Tensor Triangular Geometry''.<ref>{{cite book|last=Balmer|first=Paul|chapter=Tensor triangular geometry|title=Proceedings of International Congress of Mathematicians, Vol. II.|year=2010|pages=85–112|url=http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM2010.2/Main/icm2010.2.0085.0112.pdf|access-date=2017-10-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170811100511/http://www.mathunion.org/ICM/ICM2010.2/Main/icm2010.2.0085.0112.pdf|archive-date=2017-08-11|url-status=dead}}</ref> In 2012, he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list|title= List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society}}</ref> He was awarded the [[Humboldt Prize]] in 2015.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.humboldt-foundation.de/web/humboldt-award.html|title=Humboldt Research Award}}</ref>
